newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major hardens support for EMU free vote.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major hardens support for EMU free vote.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Thursday that allowing members of parliament a free vote on whether Britain should join a single European currency was "almost certainly" the right option.
"It is almost certainly the right way to handle it," Major told journalists at an impromptu news conference.
Major had earlier said he regarded a free vote as an option.

Major, speaking on the campaign trail ahead of the May 1 election, said if Britons were to be allowed to express their views on the issue in a referendum, it would be wrong not to allow members of parliament to exercise their judgement in the House of Commons.

If Major did allow a free vote, he might garner support from pro-European members of the opposition Labour and Liberal Democrat parties, but this would be at the cost of appearing to to be unable to control his own party. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
